0.content: Kaveh met Alhaitham, two years his junior, in the House of Daena, when he went to ask a solitary Haravatat student whether he needed help. They became close friends and research partners on a study of King Deshret's ruins. The partnership broke when Kaveh kept carrying struggling classmates and Alhaitham called his idealism a flight from reality driven by guilt. Kaveh declared he regretted ever befriending him. Years later Alhaitham found him broke at Lambad's Tavern and asked how realising his ideals had gone. Kaveh now lives in Alhaitham's house, which was converted from their old project's research site, pays rent and does all the chores. Their arguments are public, constant and mostly won by Alhaitham.

1.comment: Kaveh: The Palace of Alcazarzaray and Dori's Debt
1.content: Dori, trading as Lord Sangemah Bay, wanted a large, extravagant mansion in a secluded spot and gave Kaveh free rein on style. He talked her into a garden of carefully chosen flowers (with Tighnari's advice) and a clifftop site in the northern mountains. At 70 percent completion the Withering wiped it out overnight. He sold his family home, added his savings and covered 70 percent of the rebuild himself. The finished palace atop a great tree is called his magnum opus. He did not earn a single Mora from it and remains in debt to Dori, who reminds him whenever payment is due.

2.comment: Kaveh: Kaveh's Father and the Interdarshan Championship
2.content: About twenty years before 3.6, young Kaveh saw posters for the Interdarshan Championship and said how much he liked the prize, the Diadem of Knowledge. His father, an Rtawahist scholar, laughed and promised to win it so Kaveh could play with it. He was the favourite but lost, came home depressed, joined a desert research expedition and never returned; word came that he died in quicksand. Kaveh has lived with the belief that one sentence from him destroyed his family. A sketchbook page hidden with glue shows a figure sinking in sand with an apology to his father.

3.content: Mehrak is the green-and-white suitcase Kaveh built around a machine core from King Deshret's civilization, bought in the desert with every Mora he had on him. It hovers, carries his tools, surveys and maps sites, projects and sketches designs, grips his claymore in battle, and answers in beeps. Its name is an ancient word meaning "little light", and he hopes it can truly understand him. It understands only simple commands; he maintains it weekly and fusses over it like family.

4.content: Faranak was a brilliant, perfectionist Kshahrewar architect and Professor Zaha Hadi's student. She was beautiful, reserved and awkward with people. She raised Kaveh among block puzzles and blueprints and wrote a book called "Architectural Drawing Basics". After her husband's death she never smiled again and could not draw. When Kaveh entered the Akademiya she took a job in Fontaine, later remarried there, and left him her Sumeru property. He attended the small wedding, glad to see her smile, then came home to an unbearably empty house. They have had little contact since, and he defends her choice.
